label: ass:c11-deformations
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:c11-deformations}
Let $\mathfrak T\subset\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfy
the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
 \item[\normalfont{(i)}] The set $\mathfrak T$ is compact.
 \item[\normalfont{(ii)}] For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$, the image
 $\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\coloneqq {\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\widehat\Gamma)$ is the boundary of a bounded, simply connected
 $\mathscr C^{1,1}$ domain $\normalfont\text{D}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ with connected boundary.
 \item[\normalfont{(iii)}] For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$, the map
 ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}:\widehat\Gamma\to\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\subset\mathbb R^3$ is a $\mathscr C^{1,1}$
 diffeomorphism.
\end{itemize}
head: environment
name: Admissible boundary transformations

label: lem:c11-jacobian-multiplier
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:c11-jacobian-multiplier}
Let $\mathfrak T$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass:c11-deformations}.
For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$, the functions $J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}$ and
$J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}$ belong to $\mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Multiplication by either function is bounded on
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ for $0<\alpha<1$,
and on $H^s(\widehat\Gamma)$ for $-1\leq s\leq1$.

\label{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy}
Let $\mathfrak T$ be a set of boundary transformations
satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:c11-deformations}.
Then there exists $\delta>0$ such that the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)]
    The maps
    $\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}} \in \mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma)$ and

      \in\mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)$

      \in\mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^{3\times3})$
    admit bounded holomorphic extensions to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
\end{itemize}

label: lem:c11-sobolev-extension
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove a Sobolev estimate for $\widehat{\mathsf T}$ on its
original domain $\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$, and then
extend it by density. For this estimate, we use the Laplace single
layer BIO to define an equivalent norm on
$H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Let $\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ denote the Laplace single layer BIO on
$\widehat\Gamma$, defined, for $u\in\mathscr C^0(\widehat\Gamma)$, by 
\begin{equation}
	(\widehat{\mathsf V}_0u)(\widehat{\mathbf{x}})
	\coloneqq
	\int_{\widehat\Gamma}
	\frac{u(\widehat{\mathbf{y}})}
	{4\pi\|\widehat{\mathbf{x}}-\widehat{\mathbf{y}}\|}
	\,\,\mathrm d s_{\widehat{\mathbf{y}}},
	\quad\forall\widehat{\mathbf{x}}\in\widehat\Gamma,
\end{equation}
It is a symmetric isomorphism from
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$
to $\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ for $0<\alpha<1$
\cite[Lemma~2.5]{BonnaillieDallaRivaDambrineMusolino2018}.
Its extension to the Sobolev spaces is a bounded, positive and coercive
isomorphism from $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ to
$H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, see e.g.,
\cite[Corollary~8.13]{McLean2000}.
This extension agrees with $\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ on
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.

The operator $\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ is symmetric and coercive,
thus implying that
\begin{equation}
	(u,v)_0\coloneqq
	\langle u,\widehat{\mathsf V}_0\overline v\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma},
\end{equation}
for all $u,v\in H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, defines an inner product in $ H^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\widehat\Gamma)$
and an induced norm $\|u\|_0\coloneqq(u,u)_0^{1/2}$ that is equivalent to
$\|u\|_{H^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\widehat\Gamma)}$.
The embedding of $\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ in
$H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ is continuous.

Set $\widehat{\mathsf K}\coloneqq
\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}\widehat{\mathsf T}
\in\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
              \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))$, and let
$\widehat{\mathsf J}$ be conjugation on
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Symmetry of $\widehat{\mathsf T}$ and the real symmetric kernel of
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ give
\begin{equation}
	(\widehat{\mathsf K}u,v)_0
	=\langle\overline v,\widehat{\mathsf T}u\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma}
	=\langle u,\widehat{\mathsf T}\overline v\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma}
	=(u,\widehat{\mathsf J}\widehat{\mathsf K}\widehat{\mathsf J}v)_0,
\end{equation}
for all $u,v\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Conjugation is isometric on $\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Hence $\widehat{\mathsf J}\widehat{\mathsf K}\widehat{\mathsf J}$
is bounded and complex linear, with the same operator norm as
$\widehat{\mathsf K}$.
We apply Lax's lemma (Theorem~\ref{thm:c11-operator-extension}) with
$X=Y=\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$, the inner product
$(\cdot,\cdot)_0$, $A=\widehat{\mathsf K}$, and
$B=\widehat{\mathsf J}\widehat{\mathsf K}\widehat{\mathsf J}$,
to obtain
\begin{equation}
	\|\widehat{\mathsf K}u\|_0
	\leq\|\widehat{\mathsf K}\|_
	 {\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
	             \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))}\|u\|_0,
	\quad \forall u\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma).
\end{equation}
Since $\widehat{\mathsf T}u=\widehat{\mathsf V}_0\widehat{\mathsf K}u$
for all $u\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$, boundedness of
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0:H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)\to
H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ and norm equivalence give
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:c11-original-operator-sobolev-bound}
	\begin{aligned}
	\|\widehat{\mathsf T}u\|_{H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)}
	&=\|\widehat{\mathsf V}_0\widehat{\mathsf K}u\|_
	    {H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)}\\
	&\leq C\|\widehat{\mathsf K}u\|_0
	 \leq C\|\widehat{\mathsf K}\|_
	 {\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
	             \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))}\|u\|_0\\
	&\leq C(\widehat\Gamma,\alpha)\|\widehat{\mathsf T}\|_
	 {\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
	             \mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))}
	 \|u\|_{H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)}.
	\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The last inequality also uses boundedness of
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}:
\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)\to
\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
The constant in the last line of
\eqref{eq:c11-original-operator-sobolev-bound} reads
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:c11-sobolev-extension-constant}
\begin{aligned}
	C(\widehat\Gamma,\alpha)\coloneqq
	&
	\|\widehat{\mathsf V}_0\|^{\frac32}_{\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))}
	\|\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}\|^{\frac12}_{\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))}
	\|\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}\|_
	{\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
     \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
which only depends on $\widehat\Gamma$ and $\alpha$.

Since $\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ is the Laplace single layer BIO on the
fixed reference boundary, this constant depends only on $\alpha$ and
$\widehat\Gamma$, and is independent of $\widehat{\mathsf T}$ and $u$.
Therefore, \eqref{eq:c11-original-operator-sobolev-bound} bounds the original
operator $\widehat{\mathsf T}$ in the fractional Sobolev norms,
with the constant given in \eqref{eq:c11-sobolev-extension-constant}.

By density of $\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ in
$H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$,
estimate~\eqref{eq:c11-original-operator-sobolev-bound} gives a unique
bounded extension
$\mathcal E(\widehat{\mathsf T}):H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)
\to H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$
satisfying~\eqref{eq:c11-sobolev-extension-agreement}, with the same norm bound.
Uniqueness also implies complex linearity of $\mathcal E$.

body_md:

label: prop:c11-singlelayer-holomorphy
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the single layer BIO

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\alpha<1$.
By \cite[Lemma~2.5, item~(i)]{DallaRivaLuzziniMusolino2022}, the map
$\mathfrak T\to\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
                         \mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)):$
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf V}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$ is real analytic.
For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0\in\mathfrak T$, real analyticity gives a holomorphic
extension to a complex $\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}$ neighborhood of ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0$
\cite[Sections~5 and~13]{Mujica1986}.
Since the inclusion
$\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)
\hookrightarrow\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)$
is continuous, this extension restricts to a complex
$\mathscr C^{1,1}$ neighborhood of ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0$.
Choose this neighborhood to be a ball and shrink it so that the extension
is bounded there and every real transformation in the ball maps
$\widehat\Gamma$ onto the boundary of a $\mathscr C^{1,1}$ domain.

If two such balls overlap, their intersection is connected and
its real part contains a relatively open set. Both extensions coincide
there with the original BIO. Since
$\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)$ is the complexification of
$\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb R^3)$, uniqueness of analytic
continuation in Banach spaces
\cite[Theorem~5.34]{DudleyNorvaisa2011} shows that the extensions coincide
throughout the overlap.
A finite covering argument and the compactness of $\mathfrak T$
show that there exists $\delta>0$ such that the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf V}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:c11-jacobian-multiplier}
and~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy}, after decreasing $\delta$ if
necessary, the formula
$\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
=\widehat{\mathsf V}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}$
gives a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$ of the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))$.
Both extensions are complex Fr\'echet differentiable on $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
We use the same notation for these extensions.

For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, define the bounded bilinear form
\[
 \mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(u,v)\coloneqq\int_{\widehat\Gamma}
 (\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}u)v\,\,\mathrm d s,
 \quad u,v\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma).
\]
The map ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ is holomorphic with values in the
Banach space of bounded bilinear forms on
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)\times
\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Its antisymmetric part, i.e., the bilinear form
$(u,v)\mapsto\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(u,v)-\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(v,u)$,
depends holomorphically on ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$ in the same Banach space.
For real ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, the surface change of variables
gives~\eqref{eq:c11-symmetric-layer}, so the antisymmetric part vanishes.
Each ball $B({\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0,\delta)$, ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0\in\mathfrak T$, is contained in
$\mathfrak T_\delta$, is connected, and has a nonempty relatively
open real part. By uniqueness of analytic continuation for Banach-valued
holomorphic maps \cite[Theorem~5.34]{DudleyNorvaisa2011}, the
antisymmetric part vanishes on each ball. After decreasing $\delta$ if
necessary, these balls cover $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Thus $\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ is symmetric and
$\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:symmetry_Lax}
in Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension} for every
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, item~(ii), the extension
operation $\mathcal E$ is bounded and complex linear on the space of
H\"older operators satisfying its hypothesis~\eqref{eq:symmetry_Lax}.
Let ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$ and let
$\boldsymbol h\in\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)$ with
$\left\|\boldsymbol h\right\|_{\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)}\to0$ and
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}+\boldsymbol h\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Since ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ takes values in the closed subspace of
symmetric bilinear forms, its Fr\'echet derivative is symmetric in its
two arguments. Thus the operator
$\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}[\boldsymbol h]$
satisfies the hypothesis~\eqref{eq:symmetry_Lax} of
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}.
Since this hypothesis is linear in the operator, it also holds for the
Taylor remainder
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf R_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\boldsymbol h)
 \coloneqq
 \widehat{\mathsf U}_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}+\boldsymbol h}^{(\kappa)}
 -\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
 -\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}[\boldsymbol h].
\end{equation}
The extension estimate in Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension},
item~(ii), with $C(\widehat\Gamma,\alpha)$ given
in~\eqref{eq:c11-sobolev-extension-constant}, gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\mathcal E(\mathsf R_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\boldsymbol h))\|_
 {\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))}
 &\leq C(\widehat\Gamma,\alpha)\|\mathsf R_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\boldsymbol h)\|_
 {\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
             \mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))}\\
 &=o\bigl(\left\|\boldsymbol h\right\|_
 {\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)}\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Moreover, the map
$\boldsymbol h\mapsto\mathcal E(
\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}[\boldsymbol h])$
is bounded and complex linear. Hence the map
$\mathfrak T_\delta\to
\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):$
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathcal E(\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})$ is complex
Fr\'echet differentiable, with
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\bigl[\mathcal E(
 \widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})\bigr][\boldsymbol h]
 =\mathcal E\bigl(
 \mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}[\boldsymbol h]\bigr).
\end{equation}
It is therefore bounded and holomorphic on $\mathfrak T_\delta$.

For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, item~(iii), gives
\begin{equation}
	\mathcal E(\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})u
	=\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}u,
	\quad\forall u\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma).
\end{equation}
Since $J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}u\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$,
the same identity gives
$\mathcal E(\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}u
=\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}u
=\widehat{\mathsf V}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}u$.
Hence both extensions to the Sobolev spaces agree with their H\"older extensions on
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ for each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.
For real ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$, the extensions and the original transported
BIOs are bounded from $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ to
$H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, so density of
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ in $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$
identifies them on $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
By the preceding extension and Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy},
\[
 \mathfrak T\to
 \mathscr L\bigl(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),
                H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)\bigr):
 {\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf V}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\]
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$,
given by
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathcal E(\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}$.

title: Remark
body_md:
The scalar single layer operator denoted by $\mathsf V_{\mathbf z}$ in
\cite[Theorem~5.1]{EscapilJerez2026EFIE} corresponds to
$\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$ in our notation.
The cited result establishes its
mapping properties and holomorphic dependence in fractional Sobolev
spaces, i.e., as a map $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)\to H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, on the parameters of
affine-parametric families of boundary transformations in
$\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb R^3)$.

holomorphy with respect to the boundary transformation itself for
the compact families in Assumption~\ref{ass:c11-deformations},

label: prop:c11-double-layer-holomorphy
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the double layer BIO

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\alpha<1$.
By \cite[Lemma~2.5, items~(ii) and~(iii)]{DallaRivaLuzziniMusolino2022},
the maps
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
              \mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))$ and
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)\prime}
\in\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
              \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))$ are real analytic.
Equation~\eqref{eq:c11-scalar-pullback-duality} and
Lemmas~\ref{lem:c11-jacobian-multiplier}
and~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy} then show that
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto(\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})'
\in\mathscr L(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
              \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))$ is real analytic.
Consequently, the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}
\in\mathscr L((\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2,
              (\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2)$
introduced in~\eqref{eq:c11-double-layer-symmetric-block} is real analytic.
Arguing as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:c11-singlelayer-holomorphy}, these maps admit
bounded holomorphic extensions to $\mathfrak T_\delta$ for some
$\delta>0$ in their respective H\"older operator spaces.
We use the same notation for the extensions.

For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, define the bounded bilinear form
\[
 \mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(u,v)\coloneqq\int_{\widehat\Gamma}
 (\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}} u)\cdot v\,\,\mathrm d s,
 \quad u,v\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)\times
 \mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma),
\]
where the dot product is bilinear, without complex conjugation.
The map ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ is holomorphic with values in the
Banach space of bounded bilinear forms on
$(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2\times
(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2$.
For real ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, the block
formula~\eqref{eq:c11-double-layer-symmetric-block} and symmetry of
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ imply that
$\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(u,v)=\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(v,u)$ for all
$u,v\in(\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2$.
Its antisymmetric part, i.e., the bilinear form
$(u,v)\mapsto\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(u,v)-\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(v,u)$,
depends holomorphically on ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$ in the same Banach space and is zero
for real ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Uniqueness of analytic continuation in Banach spaces
\cite[Theorem~5.34]{DudleyNorvaisa2011} therefore shows that this
bilinear form vanishes
on each ball
$B({\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0,\delta)$, ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}_0\in\mathfrak T$, and hence on
$\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Thus $\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ satisfies the hypothesis~\eqref{eq:symmetry_Lax}
of Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, with the product of scalar
functions replaced by the bilinear dot product, for every
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.

To extend $\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ to the Sobolev spaces, we apply the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension} to two component fields, with
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0$ acting diagonally.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, item~(ii), $\mathcal E$
is a bounded, complex linear map from the operators in
$\mathscr L((\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2,
            (\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2)$
satisfying the symmetry hypothesis~\eqref{eq:symmetry_Lax}, with the
bilinear dot product, to
$\mathscr L((H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))^2,
            (H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))^2)$.
Let ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$ and let
$\boldsymbol h\in\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)$ with
$\left\|\boldsymbol h\right\|_{\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)}\to0$ and
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}+\boldsymbol h\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Here $\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\boldsymbol h]$ denotes the complex
Fr\'echet derivative of the map ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ at ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$,
evaluated in the direction $\boldsymbol h$.
Differentiating the symmetry of $\mathsf b_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ with respect to ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$
shows that $\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\boldsymbol h]$ satisfies
the hypothesis~\eqref{eq:symmetry_Lax} of
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, with the bilinear dot product.
This condition is preserved by linear combinations, so it also holds
for
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf R_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\boldsymbol h)
 \coloneqq\mathsf B_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}+\boldsymbol h}-\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}
 -\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\boldsymbol h].
\end{equation}
Complex Fr\'echet differentiability of ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$
gives the remainder estimate in the H\"older operator norm.
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, item~(ii), transfers this
estimate to the Sobolev operator norm:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\mathcal E(\mathsf R_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\boldsymbol h))\|_
 {\mathscr L((H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))^2,
             (H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))^2)}
 &\leq C(\widehat\Gamma,\alpha)\|\mathsf R_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\boldsymbol h)\|_
 {\mathscr L((\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2,
             (\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma))^2)}\\
 &=o\bigl(\left\|\boldsymbol h\right\|_
 {\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)}\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Boundedness and complex linearity of $\mathcal E$ imply that the map
$\boldsymbol h\mapsto\mathcal E(\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\boldsymbol h])$
is bounded and complex linear in $\boldsymbol h$.
Together with the preceding remainder estimate, this proves that the map
$\mathfrak T_\delta\to
\mathscr L((H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))^2,
           (H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))^2):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathcal E(\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$
is complex Fr\'echet differentiable, with derivative
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\mathcal E(\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})][\boldsymbol h]
 =\mathcal E(\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\boldsymbol h]).
\end{equation}
It is therefore bounded and holomorphic on $\mathfrak T_\delta$.

For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, define the extension to the Sobolev spaces by
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
 \coloneqq(\mathcal E(\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}))_{21}\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1},
\end{equation}
where $(\cdot)_{21}$ denotes the block in row $2$ and column $1$, and
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}\in\mathscr L(
H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$.
Taking the block in row $2$ and column $1$ and composing it with the
fixed operator $\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}$ are bounded, complex linear
operations. Hence the map
$\mathfrak T_\delta\to
\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$
is complex Fr\'echet differentiable,
with derivative
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}[\boldsymbol h]
 =\bigl(\mathcal E(\mathrm D_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}[\boldsymbol h])\bigr)_{21}
 \widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}.
\end{equation}
For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$ and
$u\in\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$, we have
$\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}u\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, item~(iii), to
$(\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}u,0)$ gives
\[
 (\mathcal E(\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}))_{21}\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}u
 =(\mathsf B_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})_{21}\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}u
 =\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}u.
\]
Hence the extension to the Sobolev spaces agrees with the H\"older extension on
$\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ for each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$.
For ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$, both this extension and the original BIO
are bounded on $H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ and agree on
$\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Density of
$\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$ in
$H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ therefore shows that they coincide on
$H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
The estimate in Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-sobolev-extension}, item~(ii),
and boundedness of $\widehat{\mathsf V}_0^{-1}$ give uniform boundedness
on $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Hence the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.

label: prop:c11-adjoint-double-layer-holomorphy
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the adjoint double layer BIO

label: eq:adjoint_DL_ref
title: Proof
body_md:
There exists $\delta>0$ such that the bounded holomorphic extensions in
Proposition~\ref{prop:c11-double-layer-holomorphy} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy} are defined on $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, we define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:adjoint_DL_ref}
	\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)\prime}
	\coloneqq J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}
	\bigl(\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}\bigr)'
	J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}},
	\quad\forall{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta.
\end{equation}
Here the prime outside the parentheses denotes the reference dual,
which is defined using the bilinear pairing, without complex conjugation.
Because the pairing is bilinear, taking the dual is a bounded complex
linear operation from
$\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$
to $\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$.
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:c11-jacobian-multiplier}
and~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy}, the maps
$\mathfrak T\to
\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\bigl(u\mapsto J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}u\bigr)$ and
$\mathfrak T\to
\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\bigl(u\mapsto J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}u\bigr)$
admit bounded holomorphic extensions to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Since operator composition is continuous and multilinear,
\eqref{eq:adjoint_DL_ref} defines the bounded holomorphic map
$\mathfrak T_\delta\to
\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)\prime}$.
For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, $\mu\in H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, and
$v\in H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, its defining pairing is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)\prime}\mu,v\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma}
 &=\langle J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}\mu,
 \widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
 (J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}v)\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$, relation~\eqref{eq:c11-scalar-pullback-duality}
identifies the right-hand side with the pairing of the transported
adjoint double layer BIO with $v$.
Since this holds for every $\mu$ and $v$ in these Sobolev spaces,
the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf K}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)\prime}
\in\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$ defined
by~\eqref{eq:adjoint_DL_ref}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta>0$ be sufficiently small so that the extensions in
Proposition~\ref{prop:c11-singlelayer-holomorphy} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy} are defined on $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-geometric-holomorphy} and the multiplier estimate
in Appendix~\ref{sec:proof_c11-jacobian-multiplier} show that the maps
$\mathfrak T\to
\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),
           \boldsymbol H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf C_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ and
$\mathfrak T\to
\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),
           \boldsymbol H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\mathsf N_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$
admit bounded holomorphic extensions to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
The map $\mathfrak T\to
\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\bigl(\widehat v\mapsto J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}\widehat v\bigr)$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$ as well.
For each ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, we define
$\widehat{\mathsf W}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$ by
\eqref{eq:c11-complex-hypersingular-definition}.
Since composition and the pairings are bounded multilinear operations,
the right-hand side defines a bounded holomorphic map with values in
the space of bilinear forms on
$H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)\times H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
The identification of bounded bilinear forms with operators therefore shows
that the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf W}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.

label: thm:c11-efie-holomorphy
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the EFIE

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:c11-singlelayer-holomorphy}, the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf U}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma),H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma))$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
The multiplier map defined above is entire and bounded on bounded sets.
The duality pairing between $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ and
$H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, and its componentwise vector extension,
are bounded complex bilinear maps. Moreover, the reference surface
divergence $\operatorname{div}_{\widehat\Gamma}:\widehat X\to H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$
is bounded and complex linear.
Identifying bilinear forms with their induced operators,
\eqref{eq:c11-efie-factorization} therefore shows that the map
$\mathfrak T\to\mathscr L(\widehat X,\widehat X'):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.

label: ass:c11-nonresonance
title: Assumption
head: environment
name: Nonresonance on closed surfaces

label: cor:c11-closed-solution-holomorphy
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the EFIE solution on closed surfaces

title: Proof
body_md:
Assumption~\ref{ass:c11-nonresonance} gives a bounded isomorphism
$\mathsf A_{\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{(\kappa)}:X_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\to X_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}'$
\cite[Sections~6 and~7.2]{BuffaHiptmair2003}.
Since the Piola transformations are isomorphisms,
$\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$ is also a bounded isomorphism for each
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$. Continuity of inversion and compactness of
$\mathfrak T$ imply that the inverses are uniformly bounded on
$\mathfrak T$. Let $\delta>0$ be such that the holomorphic operator
extension in Theorem~\ref{thm:c11-efie-holomorphy} is defined on
$\mathfrak T_\delta$. After decreasing $\delta$ if necessary, the perturbation estimate in
\cite[Proposition~4.20, item~(i)]{HS21} and continuity of the operator extension
imply that
$\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}$ is invertible for every
${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, with uniformly bounded inverses on
$\mathfrak T_\delta$.
Hence the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto(\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})^{-1}
\in\mathscr L(\widehat X',\widehat X)$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$
by holomorphy of inversion
\cite[Proposition~4.20, item~(ii)]{HS21}, with
\begin{equation}
	M_\delta\coloneqq\sup_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta}
	\|(\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})^{-1}\|_
	      {\mathscr L(\widehat X',\widehat X)}<\infty.
\end{equation}
For item~(ii), we choose $\delta\leq\delta_f$.
The bounded bilinear evaluation
$\mathscr L(\widehat X',\widehat X)\times\widehat X'\to\widehat X$
shows that
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto(\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)})^{-1}
\widehat{\boldsymbol f}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\widehat X$ admits a bounded holomorphic
extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$
\cite[Proposition~4.20, item~(iii)]{HS21}, proving item~(ii), with
\begin{equation}
	\sup_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta}
	      \|\widehat{\boldsymbol j}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\|_{\widehat X}
	\leq M_\delta\sup_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta}
	      \|\widehat{\boldsymbol f}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\|_{\widehat X'}<\infty.\qedhere
\end{equation}

label: cor:c11-closed-far-field-holomorphy
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:c11-closed-far-field-holomorphy}
Assume the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:c11-closed-solution-holomorphy}, item~(ii), and set
$\boldsymbol E_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^\infty\coloneqq
\widehat{\mathsf F}_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},\infty}^{(\kappa)}
\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\boldsymbol j_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$.
Then there exists $\delta\in(0,\delta_f]$ such that the map
\begin{equation}
	\mathfrak T\to\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3):
	{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\boldsymbol E_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^\infty
\end{equation}
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$.
In particular, the conclusion holds for the plane-wave data in
Subsection~\ref{sec:c11-closed-solution}.
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the electric far-field

title: Proof
body_md:
The map
$\mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)\to
\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\bigl(\boldsymbol\theta\mapsto
\exp(-\imath\kappa\boldsymbol\theta\cdot{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\cdot))\bigr)$
is entire
and bounded on bounded sets
\cite[Sections~5 and~13]{Mujica1986}.
The bounded embedding
$\mathscr C^{0,1}(\widehat\Gamma)\hookrightarrow
H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$, the bounded linear dependence of
$\widehat{\mathsf F}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ on ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$, and the bounded bilinear duality
between $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$ and $H^{\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$,
applied componentwise, show that
\eqref{eq:c11-reference-far-field} defines the entire map
$\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)\to
\mathscr L(\widehat X,\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3)):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf F}_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},\infty}^{(\kappa)}$,
bounded on bounded sets.
By~\eqref{eq:c11-far-field-composition},
Corollary~\ref{cor:c11-closed-solution-holomorphy}, and
\cite[Proposition~4.20, item~(iii)]{HS21}, the map
$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\boldsymbol E_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^\infty
\in\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3)$ admits a bounded holomorphic
extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$, with $0<\delta\leq\delta_f$
chosen within the neighborhood of the solution extension.

label: cor:c11-squared-far-field-holomorphy
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:c11-squared-far-field-holomorphy}
Let the assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:c11-closed-far-field-holomorphy} hold.
The maps $\Phi_{\boldsymbol\theta}:\mathfrak T\to\mathbb R$ and
$\Phi:\mathfrak T\to\mathbb R$ admit bounded holomorphic extensions
$\Phi_{\boldsymbol\theta}^{\mathbb C}:\mathfrak T_\delta\to\mathbb C$ and
$\Phi^{\mathbb C}:\mathfrak T_\delta\to\mathbb C$, respectively,
with $\delta$ as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:c11-closed-far-field-holomorphy}.
In particular, for
$U_\delta\coloneqq\mathfrak T_\delta\cap
\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb R^3)$, the maps
$\Phi_{\boldsymbol\theta}^{\mathbb C}|_{U_\delta},
\Phi^{\mathbb C}|_{U_\delta}:U_\delta\to\mathbb R$
are real analytic extensions of $\Phi_{\boldsymbol\theta}$ and $\Phi$,
respectively.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The set $\mathfrak T$ consists of real maps and its complex neighborhood
$\mathfrak T_\delta$ is invariant under conjugation.
Conjugation invariance makes the expressions
in~\eqref{eq:c11-squared-far-field-extension} well-defined.
Conjugating the local power series of $\boldsymbol E^\infty$ shows
that the map $\mathfrak T_\delta\to\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3):
{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\overline{\boldsymbol E^\infty(\overline{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}})}$ is holomorphic.
The pointwise dot product is bounded bilinear and integration over
$\mathbb S^2$ is bounded linear, so both extensions are holomorphic.
For real ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta$, we have $\overline{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}={\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$,
so both extensions are real-valued and equal the corresponding squared
norms. On $\mathfrak T$, they therefore agree with
$\Phi_{\boldsymbol\theta}$ and $\Phi$, respectively.
Writing
$M_{\infty,\delta}\coloneqq\sup_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta}
\|\boldsymbol E^\infty({\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})\|_{\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3)}<\infty$,
we obtain
\begin{equation}
	\sup_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta}
	|\Phi_{\boldsymbol\theta}^{\mathbb C}({\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})|\leq M_{\infty,\delta}^2
	\quad\text{and}\quad
	\sup_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T_\delta}
	|\Phi^{\mathbb C}({\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})|\leq4\pi M_{\infty,\delta}^2.
	\qedhere
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
In \cite[Theorem~7.3]{EscapilJerez2026EFIE}, far-field holomorphy is
proved for countably parametrized affine deformations under
interior electric nonresonance, in
$\mathscr C^m(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3)$ for every $m\geq0$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:c11-closed-far-field-holomorphy}
instead treats the deformation itself in
$\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma;\mathbb C^3)$ and yields a bounded
holomorphic extension
$\mathfrak T_\delta\to\mathscr C^0(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C^3)$.
The lack of holomorphy noted in
\cite[Remark~7.3]{EscapilJerez2026EFIE} concerns direct evaluation of
squared norms at complex parameters. Conjugation does not prevent the
construction of holomorphic functions that coincide with the squared
norms for real boundary transformations, as established by
Corollary~\ref{cor:c11-squared-far-field-holomorphy} for the functions
defined in~\eqref{eq:c11-squared-far-field-extension}.

title: Proof

label: lem:c11-screen-extension
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:c11-screen-piola-components
title: Proof
body_md:
For each $\boldsymbol j\in X_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s$,
\eqref{eq:c11-screen-scalar-transport} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-screen-scalar-operators}, item~(i), give
\begin{equation}
	\widehat{\mathsf E}^{(N)}
	    \mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s\boldsymbol j
	=\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf E_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},X}\boldsymbol j.
	\label{eq:c11-screen-piola-components}
\end{equation}
Since $\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}:X_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\to\widehat X$, the field
$\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf E_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},X}\boldsymbol j$ belongs to
$\widehat X\subset\boldsymbol H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
In particular,
$\widehat{\boldsymbol n}\cdot\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf E_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},X}\boldsymbol j=0$
in $H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
By~\eqref{eq:c11-piola-divergence} and
\eqref{eq:c11-screen-zero-extension-divergence}, its surface divergence
on $\widehat\Gamma$ is the zero extension of
$\widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}(J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}})\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s
\operatorname{div}_{\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s}\boldsymbol j$.
Since $\widehat{\mathsf E}^{(N)}$ is injective and commutes with multiplication,
$\widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}(\widehat{\boldsymbol n})
 \cdot\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s\boldsymbol j=0$
in $\widetilde H^{-\frac12}(\widehat\Gamma^s)$.
For all $\widehat\phi\in\mathscr C^{1,1}(\widehat\Gamma)$, the formula
for $\operatorname{div}_{\widehat\Gamma}
(\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mathsf E_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},X}\boldsymbol j)$ and the duality defining
$\widehat{\mathsf E}^{(N)}$ give the variational identity
\begin{equation*}
 \bigl\langle\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s\boldsymbol j,
       \widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}
          \nabla_{\widehat\Gamma}\widehat\phi\bigr\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma^s}
 ={}
 -\bigl\langle
       \widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}(J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}})\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s
          \operatorname{div}_{\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s}\boldsymbol j,
       \widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}\widehat\phi
       \bigr\rangle_{\widehat\Gamma^s}.
\end{equation*}
The variational identity shows that
$\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s\boldsymbol j\in\widehat X^s$ and
\begin{equation}
	\operatorname{div}_{\widehat\Gamma^s}
	    (\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s\boldsymbol j)
	=\widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}(J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}})\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s
	    \operatorname{div}_{\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s}\boldsymbol j.
	\label{eq:c11-screen-piola-divergence}
\end{equation}
The field formula for $\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s$,
\eqref{eq:c11-screen-piola-divergence}, and the multiplier and
pullback estimates in Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-screen-scalar-operators},
items~(i) and~(ii),
give boundedness from $X_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s$ to $\widehat X^s$.

Applying the same divergence calculation to the inverse surface
diffeomorphism ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}:\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s\to\widehat\Gamma^s$, together with
the screen multiplier and pullback estimates, gives the bounded map
\begin{equation}
	(\mathcal P_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s)^{-1}\widehat{\boldsymbol j}
	=(\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s)^{-1}
	  \bigl(\widehat{\mathsf R}^{(D)}(J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})
	         \widehat{\boldsymbol j}\bigr)\in X_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s,
	\quad\forall\widehat{\boldsymbol j}\in\widehat X^s.
\end{equation}
The tangential-projector identities
$F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}=\widehat P$ and
$F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}} F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}=\mathsf I_3-\boldsymbol N_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\boldsymbol N_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^\top$,
together with tangency and injectivity of $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^s$, show that these
maps are mutually inverse.
Since $\widehat{\mathsf E}_X$ acts component-wise as
$\widehat{\mathsf E}^{(N)}$,
\eqref{eq:c11-screen-piola-components} is
\eqref{eq:c11-screen-piola-extension}, completing the proof.

Recalling~\eqref{eq:c11-screen-piola-extension}
and~\eqref{eq:c11-screen-efie-compression}, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c11-screen-fixed-compression}

	=
	\widehat{\mathsf R}_X
	\widehat{\mathsf A}_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{(\kappa)}
	\widehat{\mathsf E}_X.

$\mathscr L(\widehat X,\widehat X')\ni\mathsf{T}\mapsto
\widehat{\mathsf R}_X\mathsf{T}\widehat{\mathsf E}_X
\in\mathscr L(\widehat X^s,\widehat X^{s\prime})$
is bounded and complex linear.

$\mathfrak T\ni{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\mapsto\widehat{\mathsf A}_{{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}},s}^{(\kappa)}
\in\mathscr L(\widehat X^s,\widehat X^{s\prime})$
admits a bounded holomorphic extension to $\mathfrak T_\delta$
by Theorem~\ref{thm:c11-efie-holomorphy}.

label: cor:c11-screen-solution-holomorphy
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Shape holomorphy of the screen EFIE solution

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\in\mathfrak T$.
By change of variables and the positive minimum and finite maximum
of $J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}$ on $\widehat\Gamma$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
	\|\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}} f\|_{L^2(\widehat\Gamma)}
	\leq C_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\|f\|_{L^2(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})}
	\quad\text{and}\quad
	\|\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}\widehat f\|_{L^2(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})}
	\leq C_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\|\widehat f\|_{L^2(\widehat\Gamma)},
\end{equation}
for all $f\in L^2(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and
$\widehat f\in L^2(\widehat\Gamma)$.
Recalling the tangential inverse $F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$,
the tangential chain rule gives, for all
$f\in\mathscr C^1(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and
$\widehat f\in\mathscr C^1(\widehat\Gamma)$,
\begin{equation}
	\nabla_{\widehat\Gamma}(\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}} f)
	=F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^\top\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}(\nabla_{\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}f)
	\quad\text{and}\quad
	\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\bigl(\nabla_{\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}
	                   (\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}\widehat f)\bigr)
	=F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-\top}\nabla_{\widehat\Gamma}\widehat f.
\end{equation}
Using these chain rules, the boundedness of $F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ and $F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$,
and the preceding estimates, we obtain
\begin{equation}
	\|\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}} f\|_{H^1(\widehat\Gamma)}
	\leq C_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\|f\|_{H^1(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})}
	\quad\text{and}\quad
	\|\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}\widehat f\|_{H^1(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})}
	\leq C_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\|\widehat f\|_{H^1(\widehat\Gamma)}.
\end{equation}
By density, these identities and bounds hold for all
$f\in H^1(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and
$\widehat f\in H^1(\widehat\Gamma)$.
By interpolation \cite[Theorem~B.11]{McLean2000}, these bounds give
boundedness of $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ and
$\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$ between $H^s(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and
$H^s(\widehat\Gamma)$ for $0<s<1$.
The identities $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}} f=f$ and
$\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}\widehat f=\widehat f$ hold for
$f\in H^s(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and $\widehat f\in H^s(\widehat\Gamma)$,
since these spaces are contained in $L^2(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and
$L^2(\widehat\Gamma)$, respectively.

For $f\in\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$,
\begin{equation}
	|f\circ{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}|_{\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)}
	\leq\operatorname{Lip}({\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})^\alpha
	      |f|_{\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})}.
\end{equation}
The seminorm estimate gives boundedness of $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ from
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ to
$\mathscr C^{0,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$.
The two surface gradient chain rules give boundedness from
$\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ to
$\mathscr C^{1,\alpha}(\widehat\Gamma)$, using the Lipschitz coefficients
$F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ and $F_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$.
Applying these estimates with ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$ and the boundaries
interchanged gives the bounds for $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$.

For $-1\leq s<0$, consider the maps
$\widehat\phi\mapsto\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}
(J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}^{-1}\widehat\phi)$ from
$H^{-s}(\widehat\Gamma)$ to $H^{-s}(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and
$\phi\mapsto J_{\text S,{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}}\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}\phi$ in the opposite direction.
Composing these two maps cancels the Jacobian factors and the
pullbacks, so each composition is the identity.
Their boundedness between $H^{-s}(\widehat\Gamma)$ and
$H^{-s}(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ follows from the
positive-order pullback bounds and
Lemma~\ref{lem:c11-jacobian-multiplier}.
By~\eqref{eq:c11-distribution-pullbacks}, $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$ and $\tau_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}^{-1}$
on $H^s(\Gamma_{\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}})$ and $H^s(\widehat\Gamma)$
are the duals of these maps. They are therefore bounded and
mutually inverse.
All constants may depend on ${\normalfont{\boldsymbol r}}$,
but not on the functions to which the operators are applied.
